title: Numbered Sentences Begin in Same Cell

illustrates.quote: When a label is followed by a numbered item on the same line, move the numbered item to the next line so all numbered items begin in the same cell. Keep the label in cell 1.

blocks.text: Mark the capitalization errors in the following sentences.

items.text: EXAMPLE: 1. The president lives in the white house.

print.notes: PDF page image (p.277) inspected directly: print shows "EXAMPLE: 1. The president lives in the white house." as ONE continuous line (the label and the numbered item on the SAME print line) — exactly the condition 10.8.5 addresses. The given braille splits them onto two separate lines ("EXAMPLE:" alone, then "1. The president...").

braille.notes: Independently re-extracted from source (fixed left margin / line-number field stripped by counting; U+2800→space; trailing spaces removed); confirmed byte-identical to both run A and run B (gold-10-A/gold-10-B) except where differences.md records a correction.
